title: onedevatlas is open: one connected graph for SAP developers
author: mike_zaschka
text:
Today onedevatlas opens to everyone. It is one connected graph of what is built for SAP development, by SAP and by everyone else: packages, plugins, services, tools, MCP servers and skills, the problems they answer, the posts and talks that explain them, and the people who make them. One graph, read by people and by their agents. 

 Why it exists 
 Building has never been easier, and being found has never been harder. On 3 October the atlas listed 31 MCP servers for ABAP. Today it lists 42. Most of them are careful work, and many solve the same problem, because their makers could not see what was already there. Agents make it sharper: an agent knows what it was trained on and what the skills beside it describe, and the work of a freelancer, a partner or a customer team is rarely part of its answer. 
 The lists we have, for CAP, for UI5, for ABAP, are good and separate. What was missing is a view across the stacks, with SAP's work and the community's side by side, and a graph underneath that says how things relate. 

 A map drawn by capability 
 Every door, CAP, UI5, ABAP and BTP, and the smaller ones for SAP Commerce, SAP SuccessFactors and SAP Digital Manufacturing, has its own map. One hexagon is one capability, a concern a project has, and its colour says who is present: SAP, the community, both, or nobody yet. Open a tile and the capability page says what SAP ships, where that stops, and who else is present. Under a capability, use cases make the options comparable by the outcome they cover and the conditions under which they cover it, never by stars or downloads. 
 Behind the map is the graph itself, at /graph : select a node and its card says what it provides, who maintains it and what it depends on, each edge with one meaning. 
 The same answers for your agent 
 The hosted MCP server at https://onedevatlas.dev/mcp answers with the same facts the pages show. This exchange was recorded against the live server today: a question about letting a coding agent change ABAP in an on-premise system lands on a capability, then on an assessed use case with seven options, six covering it under conditions and one not known, and the four things that decide between them for your system. 
 Explore, and TechEd week 
 The third way in is a flight. Explore and Play is the same graph as a place: make an orb, design a ship and fly through the ecosystems. Until Sunday 1 November, midnight in Berlin, it is shared: sign in with GitHub, meet other pilots, play rock, paper, scissors (SAP style) and collect points for what you look at. Then the boards freeze, and the leaders stay in the atlas's history. 

 Take part 
 If your work is missing or something about it is wrong, open an issue . Anything about a person goes directly through the contact form. Maintainers can sign in and write a note on their own entry. 
 The full article explains the words the atlas uses and how to read a capability page, and its discussion is open. 
 See you at TechEd, or in flight. 🚀

title: What’s New in Identity and Access Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
author: SafaBahoosh
text:
1. Overview 
 Identity and Access Management (IAM) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition provides the foundational security layer that controls user access to business applications and backend services. Traditionally, IAM apps were grouped into business catalogs, with authorization default values aggregated strictly at the catalog level. These business catalogs served as the essential building blocks for constructing business roles. The traditional authorization flow works as follows: 
 Business Role → Business Catalog → Fiori→ Authorization Defaults / Services 
 While this catalog-centric model provided a straightforward way to bundle related apps, it operated on an "all-or-nothing" principle. Assigning a catalog granted access to every application within it. 
 To solve these limitations, SAP evolved the IAM architecture from rigid catalog bundles to modular application entities. 

 2. What Is "App as Entity"? 
 Starting with Release 2502, SAP introduced “App Authorization Variants” for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. An App Authorization Variant acts as a standalone wrapper around an application's authorization requirements, decoupling it from the catalog to make the individual IAM App -rather than the catalog- the smallest assignable unit of authorization. 
 With Release 2608, this capability expands into the broader "App as Entity" framework, enabling administrators to directly assign, toggle active/inactive, and manage application access with fine-grained precision when building Business Roles. 
 The diagram below illustrates this shift from broad catalog bundling to standalone, app-level role construction. 

 2.1 The Challenges of the Catalog-Only Approach 
 While catalogs provide great pre-bundled workplaces, relying solely on them introduced friction: 
 Inability to create business roles for a specific subset of apps without custom catalog creation. 
 High change-management effort when catalogs required splitting due to evolving requirements. 
 Automatic exposure of newly added apps to end-users upon upgrades, along with their underlying authorizations. 
 By shifting to "App as Entity," administrators can now assemble roles based on exact user tasks without rigid constraints, enabling the direct launch of all application types via assigned transaction codes in S/4HANA Public Edition and SAP BTP, ABAP environment. 
 2.2 Practical Scenarios: 
 User Management: Grant user access to the Business User app without exposing access to the Business Roles app. 
 Procurement: Assign access to a specific Purchase Order app without granting permissions to all applications inside the broader Procurement catalog. 

 3. How App Assignment Works 
 "App as Entity" does not replace Business Catalogs. Instead, Business Catalogs and direct app selection run side-by-side in parallel. 
 When configuring a role in the Maintain Business Roles Fiori app (F1492), administrators now have two assignment mechanisms: 

 Assignment Type 
 How It Works 
 Best Used For 

 Assigned via Business Catalog 
 The Business Catalog is assigned to the Business Role. IAM Apps within that catalog can be selectively activated or deactivated and are part of the resulting role accordingly. 
 Standard role setup where a user needs the complete suite of applications in a functional area. 

 Direct Assignment 
 An App Authorization Variant /IAM App is selected directly for a Business Role without requiring the overarching Business Catalog to be assigned. 
 Granular role setup where a user needs only 1 or 2 specific applications from a larger domain. 
 3.1 In-App Granular Control 
 Beyond assigning broad Business Catalogs, administrators can now manage application access with pinpoint accuracy. The Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) allows security leads to directly add, remove, toggle, or inspect individual IAM Apps to match exact user job responsibilities. 
 3.1.1 Practical Example: Direct App Selection in Action 
 To see how "App as Entity" works in practice, consider configuring the "Internal Sales Representative" role as an example inside the Maintain Business Roles app. 

 As shown in the screenshot above, administrators are no longer limited to managing entire catalogs. Instead, the dedicated IAM Apps tab allows granular control over individual applications: 
 Direct App Authorization Variants: Specific apps, such as Display Business Partner , Display Customer (Centrally) , or Supplier are assigned directly as "App Authorization Variants" with their linked transaction objects. 
 Selection & Activation Control: Checkboxes alongside each IAM App let administrators select specific items to Add, Remove, Activate, or Deactivate permissions without affecting the rest of the business domain. 
 Catalog-Free Flexibility: Notice that this role has 0 Business Catalogs assigned yet contains 27 IAM Apps assigned directly. This proves that roles can now be built using standalone app entities tailored to exact job tasks. 
 3.1.2 Toggling Apps ON/OFF 
 In addition to Direct Assignment, administrators can open an assigned Business Catalog inside the Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) and toggle individual IAM Apps ON or OFF. 
 Important Note on Toggling: 
 Toggling an app OFF inside F1492 suppresses its underlying authorization defaults for that specific Business Role instance only. It does NOT alter or remove the app definition from the underlying Business Catalog in ABAP Development Tools (ADT), preserving the central catalog definition for other roles. 

 4. Application Scope: SAP Standard vs. Customer-Developed Apps 
 The "App as Entity" model applies to both SAP-delivered content and custom-built extensions: 
 4.1 SAP Standard Applications 
 As introduced in Section 2, SAP delivers standard content pre-configured as individual App Authorization Variants (SIA6 objects). 
 For standard applications, this eliminates the need to assign full standard catalogs. Security administrators can directly select individual SAP standard apps when building Business Roles, ensuring users receive access only to the exact standard functionality required for their tasks while avoiding the overhead of creating custom catalogs in ADT. 
 4.2 Customer-Developed Applications (Developer Extensibility) 
 Custom applications built via ABAP Cloud / ADT using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) are defined as External IAM Apps (SIA6 objects). 
 The Migration Requirement: To enable custom apps for individual selection in Business Roles, existing customer IAM Apps (SIA6) and their corresponding Business Catalogs (GBAK objects) must undergo a one-time migration using the built-in migration wizard in ABAP Development Tools (ADT). 
 The Outcome: Once migrated, customer-developed apps can participate in direct assignments and individual toggling just like SAP standard applications. 

 5 On-Premise (PFCG) to Cloud IAM Migration Realities 
 A common question during cloud transformation projects is whether existing On-Premise PFCG roles can be migrated directly into S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. 
 5.1 Key Architectural Differences 

 Feature 
 On-Premise (PFCG) 
 S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (IAM) 

 Primary Building Block 
 Transactions (TCODES), Auth Objects, & Profiles 
 IAM Apps (SIA6), Business Catalogs, & Business Roles 

 Menu Maintenance 
 Direct TCode insertion in PFCG Menu tab 
 IAM Apps bundled in Business Catalogs via ADT 

 Authorization Abstraction 
 Direct maintenance of Auth Objects & Fields in SU24 
 Managed via IAM Apps, Business Catalogs, and Restriction Types 
 5.2 Migration Reality 
 Because On-Premise PFCG roles lack the underlying IAM App metadata layer (SIA6 objects), there is no automated 1-to-1 role import tool. 
 Best Practice: Customers migrating from On-Premise to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition must construct their business roles using standard SAP reference catalogs or custom IAM Apps created in ADT. 

 6 Key Takeaways 
 Greater Flexibility: Security teams can build roles aligned with real user job descriptions using Direct Assignment or Catalog-based Assignment. 
 Reduced Customization: Eliminates the need to build redundant custom catalogs in ADT just to exclude a single application. 
 Segregation of Duties (SoD) Preserved: Business Catalogs remain the standard for grouping apps and preserving regularly audited SoD compliance. App as Entity adds fine-grained flexibility on top of this foundation . 
 Migration Needed for Custom Content: Existing customer-developed IAM Apps (SIA6) and catalogs (GBAK) must be migrated via the ADT wizard to participate in direct assignment. 

 7 More to read: 
 To dive deeper, explore the following official resources and reference guides: 
 Identity and Access Management (IAM) 
 Maintain Business Roles (Fiori App F1492) 
 Creating an IAM App for the Business Service 
 IAM Information System App (F2450) Usage Guide

title: E-learning Available: Driving Finance Transformation by Converting to SAP S/4HANA
author: IcyHuang
text:
For many organisations running SAP ERP, the journey to SAP S/4HANA represents far more than a technical upgrade - it is a fundamental transformation of the finance function. Legacy ERP finance architectures rely on separate data structures for financial accounting, controlling, and asset accounting, requiring complex reconciliation processes, batch-driven reporting cycles, and significant manual effort during period-end close. These constraints limit real-time financial visibility, slow down decision-making, and create a growing gap between what the business needs and what the finance organization can deliver. 
 Converting to SAP S/4HANA Finance offers the opportunity to fundamentally re-architect how financial data is captured, processed, and reported - unlocking real-time insights, simplifying the data model, and enabling a faster, more intelligent close. To help finance professionals, project team members, and consultants navigate this transformation, this 1.5-hour e-learning course guides learners through the essential finance changes, conversion activities, and data migration steps involved in moving to SAP S/4HANA Finance. 
 What You’ll Learn 
 This e-learning walks through the key finance activities involved in an SAP S/4HANA conversion, from getting your SAP ERP system ready for the move to validating data and completing FI/CO tasks after go-live. Along the way, you'll see practical system checks, real project insights, and guidance to help ensure a smooth and successful conversion. 
 The e-learning course contains below topics with an assessment at the end to test your knowledge. 
 Identify and complete key preparation activities in SAP ERP to ensure readiness for an SAP S/4HANA conversion. 
 Perform and validate finance-related conversion tasks in SAP S/4HANA, including verifying data migration to the new data model. 
 Apply FI/CO post-conversion responsibilities and best practices using insights and lessons learned from real project experiences. 
 Ready to Get Started? 
 Take the next step in your learning journey by enrolling in the Driving Finance Transformation by Converting to SAP S/4HANA e-learning course.

title: Organizational Structure in SAP TM
author: ajaybnh
text:
Why the org structure matters: 
 Every shipment in SAP Transportation Management needs an owner, someone sells the service, someone buys capacity from a carrier, and someone plans and runs the move. The organizational structure tells the system who those teams are TM fills in the right teams on your orders, sends approvals to the right people, and passes clean data to billing. Get it wrong, and you fight it on every document. I walk through how the org structure works in SAP TM, using a demo company I built called Meridian Cargo Solutions.

title: One Plan, Any Level: Customer Hierarchy Planning in SAP Revenue Growth Management
author: karenshentu
text: Key Account Managers in consumer products companies rarely plan at a single customer level — yet most planning tools still force them to. SAP Revenue Growth Management's Plan at Any Customer Level capability changes this: KAMs can now manage promotion at different customer levels (e.g. national and regional promotions) within one account plan, with level-specific commercial conditions applied automatically and overlapping activities surfaced at the point of planning — not after execution. The result is less time on plan maintenance and execution, and more time on the decisions that drive revenue. Read on to explore how hierarchy-aware planning works in practice — and how you can help shape what comes next.

title: SII Spain: error 3019 when reversing an invoice from a closed period
author: AlvaroFernandezMorales
text:
Dear community, 
 I’m working with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and the Spanish SII (received invoices, daily submission), and I’ve run into the following case. I’d appreciate it if anyone who has solved it could share their experience. 
 Scenario: A supplier invoice is posted and submitted to the SII in period A (closed, with the VAT return already filed). Later, the invoice has to be reversed for accounting reasons, and the reversal is posted in period B (open). The invoice is then re-posted correctly in period B. 
 Problem: 
 If the reversal inherits the original tax reporting date, a deregistration request is generated pointing to period A. The customer does not want a filed period to be modified. 
 If I change the tax reporting date of the reversal document to period B, the submission fails with error 3019: “El Ejercicio y Periodo del PeriodoLiquidacion deben coincidir con el último movimiento anterior”. 
 Customer requirement: The correction should be reported in the current period with the opposite sign, without manual intervention in the SII, so that the books match what has been reported. The same process should also work when the reversal falls in the same period as the original invoice. 
 What I have checked: The configuration activity for handling reversal documents (102954) offers the options “Send deregistration or set status cancelled”, “Always send deregistration” and “Send new invoice with type F1/F2/R1/R1S/R2/R2S/R3/R3S”. However, the setting is fixed per company code and document type, so it cannot distinguish between same-period and different-period reversals. 
 Questions: 
 Has anyone encountered error 3019 in this scenario, and how did you solve it? 
 Does sending the reversal as a new invoice (F1/R1) with the current period’s tax reporting date avoid the error in practice? 
 Is there a way for the standard to send a deregistration for same-period reversals and an opposite-sign entry for reversals of closed periods? 
 Thanks in advance.

title: Off-Neo migration of HTML5 Applications — Now with AI Skills
author: NachshonVagmayster
text:
Migrating HTML5 Applications from Neo to Application Frontend Service — Now with AI Skills 
 SAP Neo is approaching end of life , and if you have HTML5 applications hosted there, you already know you need to move them to the multi-cloud environment. Application Frontend service is the natural destination — it brings back the simplicity and flexibility that Neo developers valued, now built on the multi-cloud foundation. 
 While SAP Business Application Studio provides a number of tools to assist with migration, the process is still mostly manual. It can take a few hours for a simple application and up to days for a large-scale application. 
 We are happy to share a set of AI skills we built to automate most of this work. 
 Check out these earlier posts for more background about Application Frontend service: 
 Introducing Application Frontend Service 
 Simple UI Applications with Application Frontend Service 
 Moving HTML5 Applications to Application Frontend Service 
 What Are These AI Skills? 
 The skill focuses is migration from SAP Neo, but it can also migrate applications based on HTML5 Repository that use a managed approuter or standalone approuter. It targets Cloud Foundry or Kyma runtimes and supports both XSUAA and IAS authentication. 
 The package ships with three skills, each covering a different phase of the migration lifecycle: 
 /appfront:migrate analyses your existing HTML5 project, proposes a migration plan, waits for your approval, and then executes all the configuration changes. It never modifies your original project — it copies your original project to a new folder appfront-migrated/ and all changes are done to this copy. 
 /appfront:validate validates your migrated project configuration for correctness and deployment readiness. It goes through mta.yaml, xs-app.json, xs-security.json, and service bindings, and reports any issues against a known-good checklist. It can also connect to a live deployed application and validate it at runtime. 
 /appfront:cleanup is used if you want to completely roll back all changes done with the skill. It un-deploys any deployed applications and any related service instances and removes the local output folder. It always asks before any destructive step and never touches your original source project. 
 The skills are open source and available on GitHub: https://github.com/SAP-samples/html5-applications-migration-skills-for-sap-btp . 
 What Does the Skill Actually Do? 
 When you run /appfront:migrate on a Neo HTML5 project, the skill works through the migration in phases: 
 First, it reads and analyses your source files — neo-app.json, neo-mta.yaml, and manifest.json — and builds a complete picture of your routing, security constraints, and destinations. It then presents you with a migration plan: exactly which files will be created, which will be modified, and which Neo-specific artifacts will be removed. Nothing changes until you approve. 
 Once you confirm, the skill generates the full Application Frontend configuration: 
 xs-app.json — translated your neo-app.json routes and configurations 
 xs-security.json — Neo security constraints mapped to XSUAA scopes, role templates, and role collections 
 mta.yaml — with a content deployer module for deploying the application resources to Application Frontend 
 It also updates manifest.json, fixes the UI5 bootstrap path in index.html, and removes Grunt-based build artifacts that are no longer needed. 
 After generating the files, a built-in critic reviews the output against a checklist to identify common misconfigurations before you deploy. 
 Note: some steps still require manual action in the BTP cockpit — destination credentials with secrets are not exported from Neo for security reasons, so you will need to add those manually after import. 
 How Much Time Does It Save? 
 The table below provides an estimated comparison of the time needed to migrate applications manually and with the help of the AI skills, highlighting the potential time savings for applications of different sizes: 

 App size 
 Manual effort 
 Skill-assisted 
 Time saved 

 Small (1–3 routes, simple roles) 
 ~3 hours 
 ~30 min 
 ~85% 

 Medium (4–10 routes, multiple roles) 
 ~1 day (8 h) 
 ~1.5 hours 
 ~82% 

 Large (10+ routes, complex roles, WorkZone) 
 1–2 days 
 ~4 hours 
 ~75% 
 Note that end-to-end functional testing of your business logic is not included in these estimates. It requires developer or end user involvement and takes the same time regardless of how the technical migration was done. 
 Mass Migration 
 The skills support mass migration of applications. If you have multiple applications with similar characteristics, you can run the skills to migrate all of them in one go. During the process, you can consolidate applications under the same business solution and MTA deployment or keep them completely independent. Simply answer the questions presented by the skill and, if needed, provide instructions in natural language to fine-tune the migration. 
 Prerequisites and How to Get It 
 To use the migration skills, you will need: 
 AI Coding tool like Claude Code installed and connected to an LLM service 
 An SAP BTP subaccount with subscription to Application Frontend service 
 Cloud Foundry CLI installed and logged in to your target org and space 
 MBT (Cloud MTA Build Tool) installed: npm install -g mbt 
 [Optional] Application Frontend CLI (afctl) installed and logged in for fetching the application URL after deployment: npm install -g @SAP /appfront-cli 
 Detailed prerequisite list and installation instructions are available in the README file. The skills were built with Claude Code in mind, but they can be installed and used in other coding tools like GitHub Copilot. 
 Once the skills are installed navigate to your project directory and run /appfront:migrate to get started. 
 To sum up 
 If you still have HTML5 applications running in the SAP Neo environment, now is the time to migrate them to SAP multi-cloud. The good news is that, with AI skills like the ones above, the process has become much easier. 
 Give it a try and let me know in the comments how it worked for you. If you have suggestions for improvement, the best approach would be to contribute them directly to the project’s Git repository.

title: SAP Table to CDS Mapper - New Version thanks to AI-supported Development

text:
Finding a possible CDS object for a familiar SAP table is still more difficult than it should be. title: Authorization Control in Manage Maintenance Notifications via App Authorization Variants (AAVs)
author: Dhriti
text:
Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777) is the next-generation app for the maintenance notification lifecycle consolidating what previously required multiple apps — from creating a maintenance notification to screening, editing, accepting, and creating a maintenance order. 
 The same app is expected to be used by people with different responsibilities during maintenance execution, but not everyone using F5777 should be able to do the same things within it. This is exactly where authorization control can be achieved by App Authorization Variants (AAVs) . 
 This blog focuses on the different App Authorization Variants for Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777) app and how they can be leveraged for different roles. To know the fundamentals of App Authorization Variants, please refer to these blogs- SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2502: Flexible Business Role Design with App Authorization Variants and Precise Control of Fiori App Access with the App Authorization Variants . 
 The 4 AAVs of Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777)- 
 Each App Authorization Variant corresponds to a persona and defines what that persona can do inside the app. 

 AAV 
 Persona 
 Key Capability 

 F5777_EMP_TRAN 
 Maintenance Employee or Maintenance Technician 
 Create maintenance notification; edit only on request. 

 F5777_MPL_TRAN 
 Maintenance Planner 
 Employee access along with Assign/Create maintenance orders for notifications. 

 F5777_TRAN 
 Maintenance Supervisor 
 Full notification lifecycle except for Order creation/assignment — create, screen, accept, edit throughout. 

 F5777_EXCP_TRAN 
 Operator 
 Employee access along with creation of Emergency work and Minor work. 
 Let us look at each one. 
 1. F5777_EMP_TRAN | Maintenance Employee | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_EMP_PC 
 This variant is designed for maintenance employees or maintenance technicians who spot issues and raise them in the system. 
 A user with this AAV can create maintenance notifications and read all notification types. However, their ability to edit is limited. They can only edit a notification when: 
 The notification is moved to an "Action Required" subphase, 
 AND 
 Creator or the User is the or the designated Person Responsible for that notification. 
 This AAV is part of the standard role template SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE_MAINTENANCE , belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_EMP_PC . 
 Using the standard role template SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE_MAINTENANCE may enable 'Set Deletion flag' for the user due to additional business authorization coming from other catalogs in the role template. 

 Fig 1: Actions enabled for employee when notification is in Action Required subphase 
 2. F5777_MPL_TRAN | Maintenance Planner | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_MPL_PC 
 This AAV enables the maintenance planner to create notifications and allows to create or assign maintenance orders for accepted notifications. The Edit authorization is same as in F5777_EMP_TRAN AAV. This variant even allows user to delete and complete the notification. 

 Fig 2: List report view for user with AAV F5777_MPL_TRAN 

 Fig 3: Object page view when notification is created 

 Fig 4: Create and Assign Order enabled for accepted maintenance notification 
 The variant F5777_MPL_TRAN is part of standard role template SAP_BR_MAINTENANCE_PLANNER , belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_MPL_PC . 
 This role template gives additional authorizations to the user as compared to the App Authorization Variant F5777_MPL_TRAN such as- Creation of minor/emergency work, accepting, and editing the maintenance notification. 

 Fig 5: Additional actions enabled in standard planner role template for submitted maintenance notification 
 3. F5777_TRAN | Maintenance Supervisor | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC 
 A user assigned with this AAV can work with notifications across all phases — from the moment a notification is raised to when it is completed. They can create, view, screen, accept, reject, and edit maintenance notifications. Editing is not phase-restricted; the supervisor can update a notification whether it is unscreened, in action-required state, or already accepted. The user can’t create or assign maintenance order for accepted notifications with this AAV. 

 Fig 6: Object page view for user with F5777_TRAN AAV when a notification is created 
 This AAV is part of the standard role template SAP_BR_MAINT_SUPERVISOR , belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC . 
 Unlike the AAV F5777_TRAN, the standard role template SAP_BR_MAINT_SUPERVISOR offers the user to even create or assign maintenance order for accepted notifications due to additional authorizations from other business catalogs in the role template. 

 Fig 7: Additional actions enabled in standard supervisor role template for accepted maintenance notification 
 4. F5777_EXCP_TRAN | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC 
 This variant gives a user maintenance employee-level access combined with an expanded emergency and minor work creation authorization for maintenance notifications — beyond what F5777_EMP_TRAN allows, but without the screening scope of F5777_TRAN. 
 This is the most nuanced of the four, and it exists for a very specific real-world situation – the Operator role . 
 The operator use case, addressed by F5777_EXCP_TRAN, is a good example of the kind of real-world role complexity that AAVs are designed to handle — cleanly, within the standard SAP authorization model. 

 Fig 8: Maintenance employee access extended with create minor and emergency work. 
 Note: The maintenance employee can be restricted to creating either emergency work or minor work along with standard maintenance notification by maintaining restrictions in the role assigned to the user. The restriction should be applied for 'Maintenance Notification Processing Context' to support either of the options-minor or emergency. 

 Fig 9: Restriction applied for Emergency Work (01) 

 Fig 10: User can only create emergency and standard maintenance notifications 
 This is a small example of how a single app can serve very different personas through AAVs — each variant reflecting a specific set of responsibilities without over- or under-provisioning access. 
 You can see AAVs give you more precise control over authorizations, but as an admin, while designing roles, you should also consider what additional dependencies should be added to the role apart from the dependencies already proposed when adding an AAV.
